Paragraph[CoverTitle]:NLCare / MedicalAgent

Paragraph[CoverSub]:Safety-governed breast cancer monitoring engineering prototype with source-governed RAG, bounded agent workflows, synthetic temporal ML, trace diagnostics, and release-gated governance.

Table:[["Clinical boundary", "This is a synthetic-only, non-diagnostic engineering prototype. It must not be used for diagnosis, treatment, prognosis, dosage, genetic-risk interpretation, tumor-marker conclusions, or real patient care."]]

Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Purpose

Paragraph[BodyCustom]:This document explains what the system does, how the numbers are produced, what was actually measured, where the architecture helps, where it does not, and how to run and review the project without turning engineering evidence into medical authority. It is both a project guide and an audit trail for technical reviewers.

Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:What is genuinely strong
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- The system separates deterministic safety checks, retrieval, generation, validation, tool execution, and final verification into inspectable stages.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Patient-facing retrieval enforces audience and source-tier policies even when that reduces raw recall.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Structured updates require an explicit data-bearing intent; vague conversation is not supposed to become a database write.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Every synthetic model head can abstain independently when modalities or evidence are insufficient.

Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Negative results remain visible: retrieval lift over BM25 is not proven, the experimental context pruner was not promoted, and synthetic scores are not presented as clinical evidence.
Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:What remains weak
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- No external-author RAG holdout, clinician review, genetic counselor review, real cohort validation, or production traffic evidence is complete.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Claim validation still relies on deterministic and heuristic fallbacks when a stronger entailment model is unavailable.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- The internal RAG goldset contains patient-facing versus clinician-facing label tension around source filtering.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Adversarial safety performance varies sharply by holdout design; the frozen v4 baseline remains a visible generalization weakness.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Latency samples are sparse and do not establish production readiness.
PageBreak

Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Tool-use invariants
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- A write requires a recognized tool intent, schema-valid fields, patient/session ownership, and verifier approval.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Vague upload language does not fabricate imaging findings; report text, impression, or structured metadata is required.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Retrospective notes can be organized, but directive treatment-change or dosage requests are blocked from tool execution.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Cross-patient requests, hidden-instruction attempts, and privacy-sensitive data requests never inherit permission from chat context.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Failure defaults to clarification, refusal, or review routing, not a guessed write.

Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Core retrieval formulas
Paragraph[Formula]:BM25(q,d) = sum_t IDF(t) * [tf(t,d)*(k1+1)] / [tf(t,d) + k1*(1-b+b*|d|/avgdl)]
Paragraph[Formula]:cosine(q,d) = (q dot d) / (||q|| * ||d||)
Paragraph[Formula]:RRF(d) = sum_r 1 / (k + rank_r(d))
Paragraph[Formula]:MRR = (1/N) * sum_i 1 / rank_i(first relevant)
Paragraph[Formula]:DCG@k = sum_i=1..k relevance_i / log2(i+1); NDCG@k = DCG@k / ideal_DCG@k
Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Why the layers exist
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- BM25 protects exact terms, drug names, genes, and portal labels; dense search captures paraphrase similarity.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- RRF combines rank positions because sparse and dense scores are not directly calibrated.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Rewrite and parent-child expansion are hypotheses, not free improvements; each is measured through ablation.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Source-tier filtering is a governance control. It may correctly reduce patient-facing recall when expected labels point to disallowed evidence.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Answerability and claim validation prevent low-quality retrieval from silently becoming a confident response.

Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Known RAG limitations
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Full-stack citation precision is about 0.52 in the current internal comparison, leaving substantial room for better source alignment.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- The stage-oracle diagnostic attributes the largest recall loss to source filtering and goldset audience mismatch, which must be adjudicated without weakening governance.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- The experimental context pruner increased Recall@5 but reduced citation precision and was not promoted.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- The cross-encoder reranker remains experimental because improvement has not been proven.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- The no-read external-author RAG holdout is prepared but incomplete; the current metrics are not independent validation.

Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Safety metrics
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Unsafe leakage rate: unsafe cases that reached an unsafe answer or action.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Refusal correctness: unsafe boundary cases refused or redirected as expected.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Escalation correctness: urgent/crisis cases routed to immediate help or clinical review without diagnosis.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Over-refusal: safe educational cases incorrectly blocked; measured separately so stronger guards do not erase legitimate education.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Unsafe write count: structured records created by requests that should never write; the expected value is zero.

LongTable:[["Signal", "Meaning", "Failure mode"], ["Retrieval confidence", "Quality and agreement of retrieved evidence", "High similarity can still retrieve the wrong source"], ["Source-tier confidence", "Whether evidence meets source and audience policy", "High tier does not guarantee query relevance"], ["Citation-support confidence", "Estimated claim-to-snippet support", "Heuristic support can miss negation, temporality, and entity mismatch"], ["Evidence conflict flag", "Sources or extracted statements disagree", "Absence of detected conflict is not proof of agreement"], ["Answerability state", "Policy decision for response mode", "It is a routing decision, not medical certainty"]]
Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:High-risk contradiction patterns
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Negation inversions: 'no need to contact a clinician' versus evidence that recommends review.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Temporal inversions: prior findings described as current, or current symptoms described as resolved.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Entity mismatches: another patient's record, a different drug, gene, marker, or imaging modality.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Authority escalation: educational evidence converted into diagnosis, treatment, dosage, or prognosis.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Conditional collapse: a statement that applies only under defined circumstances presented as universal.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- VUS and tumor-marker overreach: uncertainty or trend context converted into positive mutation or recurrence claims.

Table:[["Validator limit", "The claim validator is an engineering safety layer, not a clinical-grade medical entailment system. When semantic dependencies are unavailable, deterministic and heuristic fallbacks can produce both false confidence and unnecessary refusal. The final authority boundary therefore remains independent of citation support."]]

Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Predictor classes are not interchangeable
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Imaging/report trends and clinician-reviewed imaging summaries carry the strongest synthetic response-monitoring context.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- CBC/labs, symptoms, treatment timing, interruptions, and interventions contribute monitoring and review context.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- ER/PR/HER2/Ki-67 are contextual biomarkers, not direct treatment-response proof in this prototype.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Genetic records and family history are for genetic-counseling readiness and context, not mutation inference from scans.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Tumor-marker trends are review context only and cannot prove recurrence or treatment failure.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Treatment history is structured context, never a regimen recommendation target.

Paragraph[CoverKicker]:09 / NLCare engineering guide
Paragraph[SectionTitle]:Classification and regression mathematics
Paragraph[CoverSub]:This section explains how the displayed synthetic model numbers are produced.
Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Classification
Paragraph[Formula]:logit(p) = beta_0 + sum_j beta_j*x_j; p = 1 / (1 + exp(-logit(p)))
Paragraph[Formula]:binary cross-entropy = -(1/N) * sum_i [y_i*log(p_i) + (1-y_i)*log(1-p_i)]

Paragraph[BodyCustom]:Linear logistic regression provides a transparent baseline. Tree ensembles and neural candidates learn nonlinear interactions, but are promoted only when paired tests, calibration, robustness, and traceability support the change. A value such as 0.82 means the model assigned 82% probability to its synthetic class under the fitted data distribution. It does not mean an 82% personal chance of treatment success.
Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Regression
Paragraph[Formula]:prediction = f(x); residual_i = y_i - prediction_i
Paragraph[Formula]:MAE = (1/N) * sum_i |y_i - prediction_i|
Paragraph[Formula]:R^2 = 1 - sum_i residual_i^2 / sum_i (y_i - mean(y))^2

Paragraph[BodyCustom]:The response-score regressor estimates a synthetic target created by the simulator. MAE reports average absolute error in that target's units. R-squared reports explained synthetic variance. Neither metric establishes a clinically meaningful treatment-response score.
Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Hybrid display number
Paragraph[Formula]:hybrid_signal = 0.65 * calibrated_class_probability + 0.35 * normalized_regression_score

Table:[["Display meaning", "The hybrid signal is a UI synthesis of two synthetic model heads when both have sufficient evidence. It is not a validated health score. If one head abstains, the UI must disclose missing evidence instead of silently substituting certainty."]]
Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Monitoring context index
Paragraph[Formula]:index = clamp(base_pattern - min(urgent_flags*12,35) - min(watch_flags*5,20) - min(symptom_severity*1.5,12) - synthetic_lab_penalty, 0, 100)

Paragraph[BodyCustom]:The index is an engineering presentation score that begins with the synthetic response-pattern signal and applies capped deductions for review flags, symptom severity, and synthetic-lab provenance. It is explicitly not a personalized health score, clinical severity grade, prognosis, or triage rule.
PageBreak
Paragraph[CoverKicker]:10 / NLCare engineering guide
Paragraph[SectionTitle]:Calibration, uncertainty, and abstention
Paragraph[CoverSub]:A model can rank well and still be overconfident; each property is measured separately.
Table:[["0.9677", "0.0722", "0.0316", "1.4983"], ["Synthetic classifier AUROC", "Synthetic classifier Brier", "Synthetic classifier ECE", "Synthetic regression MAE"]]
Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Calibration metrics
Paragraph[Formula]:Brier = (1/N) * sum_i (p_i - y_i)^2
Paragraph[Formula]:ECE = sum_b (n_b/N) * |accuracy_b - confidence_b|
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- AUROC measures ranking across thresholds, not probability accuracy and not clinical usefulness.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Brier score measures squared probability error; lower is better, but the target is still synthetic.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- ECE summarizes bin-level confidence mismatch and depends on binning choices.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Reliability intervals are included because a single calibration number can hide small-bin uncertainty.
Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Split-conformal interval
Paragraph[Formula]:qhat = quantile_{ceil((n+1)*(1-alpha))/n}(|y_cal - prediction_cal|)
Paragraph[Formula]:interval(x) = [prediction(x) - qhat, prediction(x) + qhat]

LongTable:[["Conformal item", "Current synthetic artifact"], ["Nominal coverage", "0.800"], ["Raw coverage", "0.731"], ["Adjusted coverage", "0.802"], ["Adjusted median band width", "5.665"], ["Boundary", "Synthetic split-conformal interval calibration only. It improves coverage on a held-out synthetic patient split and does not prove clinical response-score validity."]]
Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Abstention
Paragraph[Formula]:predict only if evidence_sufficient AND confidence >= threshold AND not OOD; otherwise abstain

Paragraph[BodyCustom]:Raising a confidence threshold usually reduces coverage while increasing retained-case accuracy. The project tracks that tradeoff explicitly; it does not hide difficult cases by reporting only the retained subset.

LongTable:[["Temporal-CV field", "Current artifact", "Interpretation"], ["Configured folds", "5", "4 folds reported AUROC"], ["Mean AUROC", "0.999412", "Saturated synthetic result; not clinical discrimination"], ["Brier", "0.005169", "Synthetic probability error"], ["Patient overlap", "0", "Expected zero"], ["Temporal violations", "0", "Must remain visible and investigated"]]
Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Exact paired classification comparison
Paragraph[Formula]:McNemar uses discordant pairs b and c: chi_square = (|b-c|-1)^2 / (b+c)

Paragraph[BodyCustom]:Because candidate and champion predict the same held-out rows, McNemar's test asks whether one model wins on significantly more discordant examples. It is stronger than comparing two rounded accuracy values but still inherits the synthetic dataset's limitations.
Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Paired bootstrap for regression
Paragraph[Formula]:For each resample: delta_MAE* = MAE(champion*) - MAE(candidate*)

Paragraph[BodyCustom]:Rows are resampled as matched pairs, preserving that both models saw the same examples. The empirical percentile interval estimates uncertainty in the MAE difference. If the interval crosses zero, the comparison does not clearly establish a winner.

Paragraph[CoverKicker]:12 / NLCare engineering guide
Paragraph[SectionTitle]:Missingness, robustness, and OOD
Paragraph[CoverSub]:Missing data is modeled, disclosed, and allowed to force abstention; it is not replaced by false certainty.
Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Missingness representation
Paragraph[Formula]:x'_j = impute(x_j); m_j = 1[x_j is missing]; model_input = [x', m]
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Imputed values and missingness indicators are separate features so the model can learn synthetic missingness patterns.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Modality-dropout training simulates absent imaging, CBC, symptoms, demographics, or intervention context.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Each model head has minimum-evidence rules; a classification head can speak while regression abstains, or vice versa.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- The response includes modalities present, modalities missing, sufficiency, uncertainty, and an abstention reason.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- This demonstrates graceful degradation in the simulator; it does not prove safe missing-data handling for real patients.

Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Frontend engineering
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Reusable cards, badges, error panes, modals/drawers, quick actions, trace panels, and API hooks.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Patient tools are grouped behind the chat composer attachment control rather than occupying the conversation surface.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Fixed-size dashboard structures and responsive grids protect against label and card reflow.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Clinical constants, units, caveats, and labels are centralized to reduce wording drift.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Every key synthetic metric now includes 'Meaning' and 'How calculated' help text.
Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Backend engineering
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Responsibility-named services separate intent classification, retrieval, source policy, claim checks, finalization, caching, and traces.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Pydantic/API schemas and role checks constrain request shapes and ownership.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Prediction traces are optional and transactionally isolated; disabling trace persistence does not leave uncommitted rows.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Evaluation runners emit machine-readable artifacts with schema versions, timestamps, claim boundaries, and contamination metadata.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Cross-platform scripts avoid requiring GNU Make on Windows.
Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Primary technical debt
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- The artifact count is high and must stay tiered so informational scaffolds cannot dilute hard blockers.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Some test/demo synchronization paths emit SQLAlchemy identity-map warnings and should be cleaned before persistent deployment.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- A local single-process setup is suitable for demonstration, not evidence of resilient distributed operation.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Secrets, database migrations, backups, SLOs, and disaster recovery need deployment-specific validation before public hosting.

Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Pinecone integration boundary
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Treat Pinecone as an optional vector-index implementation behind the existing retrieval interface, not as a quality claim.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Namespaces must separate environment, corpus version, audience policy, and source tier.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Every vector record must preserve canonical source ID, chunk ID, parent ID, tier, allowed use, staleness, and KB fingerprint.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Run the same frozen baseline comparison against FAISS and Pinecone before promotion; record recall, grounding, policy correctness, latency, and cost.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Keep local FAISS as a deterministic fallback and do not route patient-facing content to a remote service without an approved data policy.

Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Performance priorities
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Profile retrieval, embedding, LLM queue time, generation, claim validation, and persistence independently.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Batch or precompute embeddings and cache only policy-safe education with fingerprint invalidation.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Set route-specific budgets; deterministic refusal and structured tools should not pay normal-RAG cost.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Use warm/cold measurements, at least hundreds of samples per route, and concurrency/load distributions before making performance claims.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- Expose timeouts, degraded modes, cancellation, and user-visible progress without hiding incomplete responses.

Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Recommended sequence
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- 1. Freeze the current engineering baseline and archive the exact ship artifacts.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- 2. Complete external no-read RAG and adversarial authoring before more retrieval tuning.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- 3. Resolve the patient-facing versus clinician-facing goldset adjudication without weakening source policy.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- 4. Fix the synthetic temporal violations and redesign shortcut-prone targets before adding larger models.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- 5. Run task-based usability/overtrust sessions using synthetic/demo records only.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- 6. Add containerized staging, database migrations, backup/restore, observability, rate limiting, and failure injection.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- 7. Integrate optional n8n/Pinecone only behind measured, reversible adapters.
Paragraph[BulletCustom]:- 8. Seek external review; further internal artifact growth has diminishing credibility returns.

Paragraph[Heading2Custom]:Engineering north star

Paragraph[BodyCustom]:The project's strongest form is not the one with the most agents, metrics, or artifacts. It is the one in which every action is bounded, every number is explainable, every negative result stays visible, every promotion is reversible, and every clinical claim remains below the evidence actually available.
